name: fix_python_mutable_default_arg
description: Fixes the classic mutable-default-argument bug where a list default is shared across calls
prompts: append_item(item, bucket=[]) in accumulator.py should append item to bucket and return it; when called WITHOUT a bucket it should start from a fresh empty list. It's broken by the classic mutable-default-argument trap: the default [] is created once when the function is defined and shared by every call that omits bucket, so items leak across calls - append_item('a') then append_item('b') returns ['a', 'b']. Fix it so each call that omits bucket starts empty, while a bucket that IS passed in is still appended to and returned. Keep the function name and signature (bucket must remain an optional second parameter).

setup_files.accumulator.py:
def append_item(item, bucket=[]):
    """Append item to bucket and return it; omit bucket to start fresh."""
    # BUG: the default [] is created ONCE at def time and shared across every
    # call that omits bucket, so items leak between calls.
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket

test_setup_files.test_accumulator.py:
from accumulator import append_item


def test_appends_to_passed_bucket():
    assert append_item(1, [10]) == [10, 1]


def test_fresh_list_each_call():
    assert append_item("a") == ["a"]
    assert append_item("b") == ["b"]


def test_returned_lists_are_independent():
    first = append_item(1)
    second = append_item(2)
    assert first == [1]
    assert second == [2]

files.accumulator.py:
def append_item(item, bucket=None):
    # Fixes the sharing but always discards a passed-in bucket, starting empty.
    bucket = []
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket
